verses.text: He who isolates himself pursues selfish desires; he rebels against all sound judgment.

xrefs.text: Pay careful attention, then, to how you walk, not as unwise but as wise,
I never sat with the band of revelers, nor did I celebrate with them. Because Your hand was on me, I sat alone, for You have filled me with indignation.
It is honorable for a man to resolve a dispute, but any fool will quarrel.
My son, if you accept my words and hide my commandments within you,
My son, fear the LORD and the king, and do not associate with the rebellious.

verses.text: A fool does not delight in understanding, but only in airing his opinions.

xrefs.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and discipline.
A shrewd man keeps his knowledge to himself, but a foolish heart proclaims its folly.
Why should the fool have money in his hand with no intention of buying wisdom?
Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, or set foot on the path of sinners, or sit in the seat of mockers.
Every prudent man acts with knowledge, but a fool displays his folly.

verses.text: With a wicked man comes contempt as well, and shame is accompanied by disgrace.

xrefs.text: If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you.
Drive out the mocker, and conflict will depart; even quarreling and insults will cease.
When the wicked thrive, rebellion increases; but the righteous will see their downfall.
When pride comes, disgrace follows, but with humility comes wisdom.
Because of this, they consider it strange of you not to plunge with them into the same flood of reckless indiscretion, and they heap abuse on you.

verses.text: The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook.

xrefs.text: The intentions of a man’s heart are deep waters, but a man of understanding draws them out.
The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer everyone.
But whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give him will become in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life.
The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one from the snares of death.

verses.text: Showing partiality to the wicked is not good, nor is depriving the innocent of justice.

xrefs.text: You must not pervert justice; you must not show partiality to the poor or favoritism to the rich; you are to judge your neighbor fairly.
Do not deny justice or show partiality. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
“How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked? Selah
To show partiality is not good, yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.
These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judgment is not good.

verses.text: A fool’s lips bring him strife, and his mouth invites a beating.

xrefs.text: A stone is heavy and sand is a burden, but aggravation from a fool outweighs them both.
Do not make friends with an angry man, and do not associate with a hot-tempered man,
A worthless man digs up evil, and his speech is like a scorching fire.
Arrogance leads only to strife, but wisdom is with the well-advised.
A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again.

verses.text: A fool’s mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a snare to his soul.

xrefs.text: He who guards his mouth protects his life, but the one who opens his lips invites his own ruin.
An evil man is trapped by his rebellious speech, but a righteous man escapes from trouble.
The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of the fool invites destruction.
They will be made to stumble, their own tongues turned against them. All who see will shake their heads.
May the heads of those who surround me be covered in the trouble their lips have caused.

verses.text: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.

xrefs.text: Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
A perverse man spreads dissension, and a gossip divides close friends.
You must not go about spreading slander among your people. You must not endanger the life of your neighbor. I am the LORD.
Without wood, a fire goes out; without gossip, a conflict ceases.
Your tongue devises destruction like a sharpened razor, O worker of deceit.

verses.text: Whoever is slothful in his work is brother to him who destroys.

xrefs.text: Idle hands make one poor, but diligent hands bring wealth.
Then you will not be sluggish, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised.
I went past the field of a slacker and by the vineyard of a man lacking judgment.
Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.
Do not join those who drink too much wine or gorge themselves on meat.

verses.text: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.

xrefs.text: My God is my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield, and the horn of my salvation. My stronghold, my refuge, and my Savior, You save me from violence.
Trust in the LORD forever, because GOD the LORD is the Rock eternal.
I will say to the LORD, “You are my refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust.”
He is my steadfast love and my fortress, my stronghold and my deliverer. He is my shield, in whom I take refuge, who subdues peoples under me.
For You have been my refuge, a tower of strength against the enemy.

verses.text: A rich man’s wealth is his fortified city; it is like a high wall in his imagination.

xrefs.text: The wealth of the rich man is his fortified city, but poverty is the ruin of the poor.
For wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.
Surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin; He will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent; He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah
Then I will say to myself, “You have plenty of good things laid up for many years. Take it easy. Eat, drink, and be merry!
Riches are worthless in the day of wrath, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.

verses.text: Before his downfall a man’s heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.

xrefs.text: The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom, and humility comes before honor.
Young men, in the same way, submit yourselves to your elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because, “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
When pride comes, disgrace follows, but with humility comes wisdom.

“Son of man, tell the ruler of Tyre that this is what the Lord GOD says: Your heart is proud, and you have said, ‘I am a god; I sit in the seat of gods in the heart of the sea.’ Yet you are a man and not a god, though you have regarded your heart as that of a god.
Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

verses.text: He who answers a matter before he hears it— this is folly and disgrace to him.

then you must inquire, investigate, and interrogate thoroughly. And if it is established with certainty that this abomination has been committed among you,
It is a trap for a man to dedicate something rashly, only later to reconsider his vows.
I was a father to the needy, and I took up the case of the stranger.

verses.text: The spirit of a man can endure his sickness, but who can survive a broken spirit?

xrefs.text: A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance, but sorrow of the heart crushes the spirit.
A joyful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones.
But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness. Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.
In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while you may have had to suffer grief in various trials
He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.

verses.text: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks it out.

xrefs.text: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to him.
A discerning heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.
let the wise listen and gain instruction, and the discerning acquire wise counsel
Instruct a wise man, and he will be wiser still; teach a righteous man, and he will increase his learning.
She had a sister named Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message.

verses.text: A man’s gift opens doors for him, and brings him before great men.

xrefs.text: Many seek the favor of the prince, and everyone is a friend of the gift giver.
A bribe is a charm to its giver; wherever he turns, he succeeds.
Now let this gift your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who follow you.

But Jacob insisted, “No, please! If I have found favor in your sight, then receive this gift from my hand. For indeed, I have seen your face, and it is like seeing the face of God, since you have received me favorably.

Then their father Israel said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: Put some of the best products of the land in your packs and carry them down as a gift for the man— a little balm and a little honey, spices and myrrh, pistachios and almonds.

verses.text: Casting the lot ends quarrels and separates strong opponents.

xrefs.text: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.

Now the leaders of the people settled in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to live in the holy city of Jerusalem, while the remaining nine were to dwell in their own towns.
Then Saul said, “Cast the lot between me and my son Jonathan.” And Jonathan was selected.
The Merarites, according to their clans, were allotted twelve cities from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.

As their brothers the descendants of Aaron did, they also cast lots in the presence of King David and of Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the families of the priests and Levites— the family heads and their younger brothers alike.

verses.text: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a castle.

xrefs.text: He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.

Now Israel loved Joseph more than his other sons, because Joseph had been born to him in his old age; so he made him a robe of many colors.

verses.text: From the fruit of his mouth a man’s belly is filled; with the harvest from his lips he is satisfied.

xrefs.text: An evil man is trapped by his rebellious speech, but a righteous man escapes from trouble.
A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
From the fruit of his lips a man enjoys good things, but the desire of the faithless is violence.
for it is pleasing when you keep them within you and they are constantly on your lips.

verses.text: Life and death are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.

xrefs.text: Let no unwholesome talk come out of your mouths, but only what is helpful for building up the one in need and bringing grace to those who listen.
The good man brings good things out of his good store of treasure, and the evil man brings evil things out of his evil store of treasure.
Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer everyone.
When words are many, sin is unavoidable, but he who restrains his lips is wise.
The tongue also is a fire, a world of wickedness among the parts of the body. It pollutes the whole person, sets the course of his life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.

verses.text: He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.

xrefs.text: Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.
A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.
A wife of noble character is her husband’s crown, but she who causes shame is like decay in his bones.
Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun— all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.
But because there is so much sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.

verses.text: The poor man pleads for mercy, but the rich man answers harshly.

xrefs.text: If you lavish attention on the man in fine clothes and say, “Here is a seat of honor, but say to the poor man, “You must stand or “Sit at my feet,
The brother in humble circumstances should exult in his high position.
But you have dishonored the poor. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into court?
But Pharaoh replied, “Who is the LORD that I should obey His voice and let Israel go? I do not know the LORD, and I will not let Israel go.”

Now the wife of one of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, “Your servant, my husband, is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. And now his creditor is coming to take my two children as his slaves!”

verses.text: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.

xrefs.text: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.
Oil and incense bring joy to the heart, and the counsel of a friend is sweetness to the soul.
I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were delightful to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.

Then Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul and said to him, “The king should not sin against his servant David; he has not sinned against you. In fact, his actions have been highly beneficial to you.
